title: VerifyPromotionReady._loadAndValidateProgressFile trusts a progress file whose write-side entries are stamped during forge's LOCAL pass
fingerprintNote: Carried VERBATIM from classified-findings.json; not recomputed by finding-manager.
description: The verifier guards against 'a verifier run against a file the cutover never finished writing' with `require(_isDeployed("NudgeStreamer") && _isDeployed("BatchNFTMinter"), "Progress file is missing core deployment records - the cutover did not complete. Resume it before verifying")`. Those records cannot signal dispatch completion: `_trackDeployment`/`_trackConfig` call `_writeProgressFileWithStatus("in_progress")` on EVERY step (:2161, :2169) and run() flips it to "completed" at :435 — all inside forge's single local pass, before transaction #1 is signed. On a partial broadcast the file therefore already exists, already carries all 14 addresses, and already says "completed". The gate can only distinguish 'the local pass aborted early' from 'the local pass succeeded' — a pre-broadcast condition, not the post-broadcast one it names. The verifier also never reads `deploymentStatus` at all (only scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js:122 does).
impact: None. No assets, no availability, no on-chain state. The impact is diagnostic quality on the contract built to be the cutover's safety net.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. Precondition: the broadcast partially applies (a mid-sequence revert or a signing interruption).

2. Because _trackDeployment/_trackConfig call _writeProgressFileWithStatus('in_progress') on EVERY step (:2161, :2169) and run() flips it to 'completed' at :435 — all inside forge's single LOCAL pass, before transaction #1 is signed — the progress file already exists, already carries all 14 addresses, and already reads 'completed'.

3. The operator runs `:verify`. Its gate `require(_isDeployed('NudgeStreamer') && _isDeployed('BatchNFTMinter'), 'Progress file is missing core deployment records - the cutover did not complete. Resume it before verifying')` PASSES, because record presence is a pre-broadcast fact.
4. The run proceeds past a gate that told the operator the cutover completed when it did not.
5. _phase7_wiringAssertions() then runs against LIVE CHAIN STATE and fails loudly — the incompleteness IS detected, just with a worse and later message than the named gate implied.
likelihood: low-to-medium as a condition (any partial broadcast triggers it), but the outcome is bounded to message quality because the real detector is intact.
justification: Low, on exactly the basis the deduplicator established and no more. This is NOT an incompleteFixOf run-22 M-01 and is not graded as one: the fix's actual detection mechanism, _phase7_wiringAssertions() against live chain state, works and fires. The defect is confined to one require whose message claims a post-broadcast guarantee it structurally cannot provide — so an operator reading 'the cutover did not complete' as the thing that would have stopped them is misinformed about which control is protecting them. That earns Low rather than QA for two reasons: it sits inside the safety-net contract itself, where a guard overstating its own coverage is worse than elsewhere (project memory: falsely-exhaustive self-certification RAISES severity rather than sanitizing), and it is the SEVENTH consumer of the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast idiom flagged in run-22's MR-22-01 recall gap — which the project's own package.json:289 documents in its own words as 'after a crash IT LIES'. A defect the project has written down and then re-instantiated inside its own safety net is a systemic signal, not a nit. It does not reach Medium: nothing is lost, nothing becomes unavailable, and the incomplete cutover is still caught.
recommendation: Make the gate read something only DISPATCH can produce. Preferred: have the verifier require `deploymentStatus == 'completed'` AND independently confirm on-chain code at the recorded NudgeStreamer and BatchNFTMinter addresses (`addr.code.length > 0`). That costs two staticcalls and turns the guard honest, because bytecode at a recorded address cannot exist unless a transaction actually landed. Alternative: drop the misleading require entirely and let Phase 7 be the sole authority, with a comment explaining why a pre-dispatch record check is impossible. Do NOT leave the current wording in place with a comment — the message is what misleads.
classSiblingDisclosure: Same family as open ledger entry L-03 (ea648ec5…, Low, open) but not a duplicate: L-03's gate reads the `deploymentStatus` STRING from JS with an off-chain blast radius, while this finding establishes that the verifier never reads `deploymentStatus` AT ALL and gates on record PRESENCE instead. The two gates share no input and neither accepted fix touches the other. NOTE for the report-writer: recommendation option (a) here WOULD start reading `deploymentStatus`, so if L-03's accepted fix (restate the header honestly) lands first, the two must be sequenced — fix L-03's header semantics before making this verifier depend on that string.
recallGapDisclosure: MR-22-01 (run-22 cross-run recall gap) counted six users of the _writeProgressFileWithStatus local-pass idiom across the mainnet cutover scripts. This is the seventh, and the first inside a contract introduced specifically to close a verification gap. Recorded so the gap is not narrowed by omission — it widened. The report-writer should carry this sentence.
